# Schema-Free Text-to-SQL: Learning Enterprise Database Structure from Query Logs

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#schema-free-query-logs)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.33946v1) · arXiv:2610.33946v1, 24 October 2026

**Reading coverage:** All fourteen PDF pages, Sections 1-8 and Appendices A-H, prompts, graph adaptation, per-domain tables and all example/rubric analyses.

## Research question

Enterprise terminology and implicit joins can defeat retrieval based only on similarity to poorly documented schemas.

## Method

The enterprise pipeline mines table usage and joins from query logs, generates metadata/entities, and retrieves through entity matching, graph traversal and ranking. Retrieved metadata, paths and historical examples condition SQL generation.

## Evaluation

The internal study uses 240 tables, roughly 500,000 logs and 35 test questions, assessed by two engineers and LLM judges. BEAVER evaluates 209 questions but constructs its graph from supplied schema metadata and inferred joins because logs are unavailable.

## What the results support

The BEAVER adaptation improves SQL execution validity from 60.8% to 95.7% over the stated RAG baseline. Pairwise/rubric preference supports better retrieval in tested settings; these are not gold-execution correctness rates.

## Limits and qualifications

Public results do not test log-derived schema discovery. Human-judge agreement is measured on clear-preference internal cases, not all BEAVER judgments. Open-ended question labels and semantic quality scores are model-mediated. Running SQL and receiving high rubric scores do not establish intended answers, complete ambiguity resolution or refusal capability.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Separates missing documentation from language ambiguity and motivates careful reporting of retrieved-context and evaluation conditions.

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.
